newsitem.title: CHILE: Codelco reaches 2nd settlement in futures scandal.
newsitem.headline: Codelco reaches 2nd settlement in futures scandal.

text.p: Chile's state copper company Codelco said local mining firm Compania Minera El Bronce will pay it $6.4 million to settle a dispute over futures deals carried by ex-Codelco operator Juan Pablo Davila.

"Minera El Bronce will pay Codelco $6,426,000 for differences between the market price and the price received or paid by Codelco as the result of operations carried out through Codelco's futures department by ex-operator Juan Pablo Davila," said the statement.
The deal comes four months after Merrill Lynch agreed to pay Codelco $25 million to end wrangling over its involvement in Davila's failed deals which cost Codelco $175 million in 1993.
Minera El Bronce is owned by the family of former Codelco CEO Alejandro Noemi who resigned in disgrace after the losses were revealed in early 1994.
El Bronce's links with Davila were only uncovered last year after the former trade gave details of the deals to Chilean investigators.
